decode: arg0=utf8
arg0 is the Riot Client's Config\lockfile as WindowsRiotLocalLaunch.launch in src/main/launchers/riot/local-launch.ts reads it (readFileSync utf8: a BOM stays as U+FEFF, invalid bytes become U+FFFD).
No lockfile is in the fixtures (a real one is never read here, docs/adapters/riot.md rule 4); every input is the test file's placeholder lockfile or a change to it, and every password is a placeholder.
The text is trimmed with JS String.prototype.trim (which removes U+FEFF and keeps U+0085) before it is split on ":".
The port limits are the function's own: 1 to 65535, at most five ASCII digits; the cases sit at and one past each.

unicode-space: a UTF-8 BOM before the lockfile: JS trim removes U+FEFF, so the name matches; Rust str::trim keeps U+FEFF
unicode-space: a trailing U+0085: JS trim keeps it, so the protocol is not https; Rust str::trim removes U+0085
unicode-space: U+00A0, U+3000, U+2028 and U+205F around the line; both trims remove them
unicode-digit: the port in Arabic-Indic digits: JS \d is ASCII only and refuses it; a Unicode \d would take it
unicode-digit: the pid in fullwidth digits: JS \d refuses it
parseint: a port of +80: Number would take it, the digit check refuses it first
parseint: a port of 0x50: Number would read 80, the digit check refuses it first
parseint: a port of 08080: Number reads it as decimal 8080, never octal
utf8-decode: a lone 0xFF and a CESU-encoded surrogate (ED A0 80) in the password; Node gives one U+FFFD for the first and three for the second
utf16-length: an astral character in the password is kept whole
utf8-decode: the placeholder lockfile ending in a truncated three-byte sequence after the protocol: Node gives one U+FFFD, which trim keeps, so the protocol is not https
